title: What If the Sun Drifted Into a Cold Interstellar Cloud?

scenes.text: What if the Sun drifted out of its protective bubble? Scientists think it may already have.
A bubble of solar wind called the heliosphere shields the planets from the dense gas between the stars.
A 2024 Nature Astronomy study found the Sun may have crossed a cold, dense cloud 2 to 3 million years ago.
In their simulations, that cloud squeezed the heliosphere to smaller than Earth's orbit.
Earth would have been briefly exposed to the raw interstellar medium. Iron-60 and plutonium-244 on Earth fit that story.
Whether it chilled the climate is only a proposal. The authors put the odds of the crossing at about 1.3 percent.
